decisions.question: From S09 the orchestrator stamped its own decisions (DEC-186, 187, 193, 234, 246, 310) and the S10 to S16 run lines with local time (UTC+7) labelled as UTC, about seven hours late. The ledger is append-only. How is it corrected?

options.label: Rewrite the affected lines
options.consequence: The ledger reads right, at the cost of breaking its append-only rule and the commits that recorded the original lines.

options.label: Publish a correction file and guard the tool
options.consequence: The ledger stays append-only; docs/auto-run/timestamp-corrections.md gives each affected entry its commit-time bounds; ledger.mjs now rejects any time later than the clock, so the error cannot recur silently.

decisions.chosen: Publish a correction file and guard the tool
decisions.why: The decision schema says ledger lines are never edited or removed, and the owner's review is pinned to them. The true times are recoverable from git commit times, which the machine clock wrote, so a correction file loses nothing. The cause was hand-written stamps after a date-change notice that reported the local date; every stamp now comes from date -u.
